personality_one_liner: High-contrast, utilitarian ride-sharing interface optimized for single-handed use, glanceable maps, and native-feeling fluid interactions.

spacing.rule: Generous spacing. Keep floating UI (FABs, Back buttons) safely off the edges (lg or xl spacing). Bottom sheets must account for home indicator safe area.

do's: Use blur on the floating back buttons and floating action buttons over the map.
Use subtle glass effect on the bottom sheet header drag handle area if background content scrolls.
Use frosted glass on custom sticky map markers.
dont's: Don't use glass on list items, form inputs, or primary CTA buttons.
Don't stack glass on top of glass.

screens.name: Rider Home
screens.purpose: Map-centric discovery and ride booking entry point.

states.loading: Map skeleton or grey map with centered spinner.
states.empty: No drivers nearby alert banner overlay.

screens.layout: 60-70% Viewport is `MapView` (absolute background). Floating Action Button (FAB) at top-left for drawer/profile. FAB at bottom-right for 'My Location'. A permanent `@gorhom/bottom-sheet` sits at the bottom. Inside sheet: 'Where to?' input field triggering address search (Alwar Junction, Kala Kuan, etc.). Once destination is set, the sheet expands to show horizontally scrollable Vehicle Options (Nafis Bike, Nafis Auto) with ETA and Fare, followed by a sticky, full-width `brandPrimary` 'Book Ride' CTA at the bottom.

screens.name: Rider Ride Status
screens.purpose: Live tracking of assigned Captain and trip progress.

states.loading: Finding Captain pulsing animation on map.
states.error: Trip cancelled or driver unavailable notice.

screens.layout: MapView background with live polyline. Minimized floating trip state chip at the top ('Arriving in 3 mins'). Bottom sheet locked at `md` snap point containing: Driver Avatar, Name, Vehicle Plate (highly legible), rating. Secondary actions (Call, Share, Cancel) arranged horizontally as pill buttons. ETA progress bar. Must use WebSocket or fast-polling simulation.

screens.name: Captain Home
screens.purpose: Shift management, map overview, and earnings snapshot.

states.empty: Offline state: Map is greyed out/blurred, zero earnings shown.

screens.layout: Map background. Massive, unmistakable Online/Offline toggle at the top safe area (safe, glanceable). When online, map is active. Bottom sheet shows 'Today's Earnings' summary. High contrast, oversized tap targets. Needs an explicit 'Offline' visual mode (e.g., desaturated map) so Captains know they won't get requests.

screens.name: Captain Ride Request Modal
screens.purpose: High-urgency interrupt to accept a new ride.
screens.layout: Full-screen or 80% height bottom sheet that slides up with a sound/haptic alert. Dark or high-contrast background to demand attention. Prominent Pickup and Dropoff locations (e.g., Matsya Industrial Area). Estimated payout in massive typography. Countdown timer bar shrinking. Swipe-to-accept or large press-and-hold 'Accept Ride' button to avoid accidental taps.

screens.name: Admin Dashboard
screens.purpose: Platform oversight, user management, and fare config.

states.empty: No active rides or pending captains.
states.error: Failed to fetch metrics, retry button.

screens.layout: Non-map, utility-first list view. Stack navigation. Top section: Quick stat cards (Active Captains, Live Rides) using 2-col grid. Below: list of recent actions or tabs for 'Users', 'Captains', 'Rides'. List rows are clean, using `surfaceSecondary` with status chips (`success` for approved, `error` for blocked). Floating action button to modify base fare.

map_placeholder.alt: Abstract night map view for placeholders

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly follow the color palette: Golden Yellow (#FFCC00) and Dark Slate (#222222). Do not introduce blues, purples, or indigos anywhere in the app.

Implement the Rider Home screen with `@gorhom/bottom-sheet` and `react-native-maps`. The map must be the absolute background (`flex: 1` or `StyleSheet.absoluteFillObject`), with the bottom sheet layering over it.
For the bottom sheet over the map, ensure you handle safe area insets at the bottom so the 'Book Ride' button isn't hidden by the home indicator.
On the Captain Ride Request Modal, implement a countdown timer (simulated UI) and a massive 'Accept' action. Use haptics heavily here to simulate the alert.
Implement clear Loading, Empty, and Error states as defined for every data-fetching screen.
Ensure touch targets are at least 44x44pt.
For the Admin dashboard, keep the layout dense and utilitarian (like 'Dark-First Utility' but using the light/dark tokens defined). Rely on status chips for visual parsing.
